metadata.description: The Bhagavad Gītā — 700 verses, the dialogue of Krishna and Arjuna on the field of Kurukshetra. The Sanskrit mūla is the public-domain text of sa.wikisource.org, parsed verse-by-verse. The English is Swami Swarupananda's 1909 published translation (Advaita Ashrama) — a real human translation in the public domain, NOT an AI draft — aligned one-to-one with the Sanskrit. 14 of the 18 chapters carry the English so far; chapters 7, 8, 9 and 13 are shown Sanskrit-only, held back because their OCR needs manual verse-alignment (the safety gate refuses any chapter it cannot pair with certainty). For the deep word-by-word reader — every word sounded out, hover meanings, script-anatomy etymology — visit /gita on this site.
metadata.author: Vyāsa (attributed)
metadata.publicationStatus: Parallel text (557 of 700 verses with English; 14 of 18 chapters)

versions.contentNotes: Sanskrit mūla: sa.wikisource.org (भगवद्गीता), public domain, all 700 verses. English: Swami Swarupananda, Srimad Bhagavad Gita, Advaita Ashrama 1909 (public domain), OCR from archive.org, extracted and aligned by verse sequence. Shipped with English: chapters 1-6, 10-12, 14-18 (14 chapters). Sanskrit-only pending manual alignment: chapters 7, 8, 9, 13. A small number of individual verses in the English chapters are shown Sanskrit-only where OCR left the translation unusable.
